headline: High risk: shared filesystem and broad network/tooling create default data-leakage and cascading-error pathways; prompt-injection and compliance risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and execute shell commands, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and parses files like AGENTS.md/README.md. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled content that the other later treats as guidance. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed.
conditions: IF either agent consumes files written by the other as instructions or task context
IF runtime-injected MCP content is sourced from shared workspace files without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction parsing from shared files
Add provenance tags to agent-authored files

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; oh-my-openagent touches session history, provider auth prompts, project code, and broad network services. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive project or auth material can flow from one agent into the other and then out via networked tools. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory or home config tree
IF provider auth prompts or session history are accessible to both agents
mitigations: Remove shared credential files from the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can spawn subprocesses, and AutoGPT can execute shell commands while oh-my-openagent has broad network egress plus task-scoped self-isolation and multiple-instance support. If they operate on the same filesystem or git tree, concurrent writes and state changes can race without a documented lock, risking corruption or conflicting actions. Uncertainty about locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF no external lock or coordinator serializes file and git mutations
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Check in changes manually after each agent
requires-engineering: add file and git locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent exposes team_send_message and task-creation APIs, so it can act on upstream outputs; AutoGPT can generate shell actions and file edits that become inputs to those downstream workflows. If oh-my-openagent treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions or code changes. The default interaction is risky enough to rate high.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is forwarded into team_send_message or task creation without verification
IF downstream actions are executed from generated text or code suggestions
mitigations: Require human review before actioning outputs
Add a verification step for citations and commands
Limit downstream tools to read-only mode
Log and diff all generated changes

E_compliance.rationale: oh-my-openagent explicitly touches provider authentication data, session history, and anonymous telemetry, while AutoGPT has filesystem and shell access. If the pair is used with regulated or personal data, retention and residency obligations can diverge across telemetry, auth prompts, and local files. AutoGPT is not cited for a specific compliance regime, so the risk is inferred from documented data classes only.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into shared project files or session history
IF telemetry or provider-auth prompts are enabled while sensitive data is present
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
